<SPAN 6>1. <SPAN 8>2. <SPAN 16>4. Time Period. </SPAN 16><SPAN 17>The nondisclosure provision of this Agreement shall survive the termination of this Agreement and Receiving Party’s duty to hold Confidential Information in confidence shall remain in effect indefinitely.</SPAN 17>
<SPAN 18>5. guidance.when: The source expressly makes return or destruction of protected information operative upon termination, expiration, rejection, or conclusion of the agreement, project, or contemplated relationship.
guidance.inspection: Separate the operative return or destruction duty from request-only duties, then verify that the stated trigger is an ending event and carry forward any scope limits or exceptions.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the ending-event trigger together with the operative return or destruction language; include a governing list introduction when the duty is an item.

guidance.when: The source expressly exempts identified copies or stored protected information from a return or deletion duty and permits their continued retention.
guidance.inspection: Read the general return or destruction rule with every overriding exception; identify what may remain, who or what system may hold it, its purpose, and continuing restrictions.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the retention permission and any governing exception transition, plus material limits such as archival-only access, dispute purpose, or continuing confidentiality.

guidance.when: The source expressly prohibits disclosure of the existence or occurrence of negotiations, discussions, an agreement in progress, receipt of evaluation material, or terms or status of the contemplated transaction.
guidance.inspection: Distinguish secrecy of the deal process or agreement facts from ordinary secrecy of confidential information, and preserve consent, audience, and publicity qualifications.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the prohibition's governing language and each relied-on enumerated subject; a generic nondisclosure clause alone is insufficient.

guidance.when: A source clause expressly addresses making, reproducing, automatically creating, returning, destroying, or retaining copies of protected information.
guidance.inspection: Classify the copy language by legal function: affirmative exception, automatic-copy acknowledgement, consent-conditioned prohibition, mere reference to existing copies, return duty, or retention carve-out. Do not infer creation permission from employee access or generic safeguarding.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative copy wording and its governing condition or exception; read adjacent retention or return language when it changes the clause's function.

guidance.when: The source expressly states that the agreement or disclosure grants, conveys, or confers no right or license in protected information or associated intellectual property.
guidance.inspection: Identify the denied grant separately from ownership, limited-purpose use, and review permissions; preserve any express narrow exception without treating it as a general license.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative no-rights or no-license wording and any material exception; ownership language may be retained as independent support but is not a substitute for an express grant denial.

guidance.when: The source expressly limits use of protected information to a stated agreement, transaction, evaluation, project, discussion, or business-relationship purpose, whether phrased as 'only' or as a prohibition with a necessary-purpose exception.
guidance.inspection: Treat the permitted purpose as the boundary of the restriction, not as permission for unrelated uses; capture both affirmative only-use wording and complementary other-purpose prohibitions.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative use limitation and the text identifying the permitted purpose; include a governing introduction when the rule is listed.

guidance.when: The source expressly permits creating copies needed for a stated purpose or acknowledges an automatic copying process and permits the resulting copies to exist.
guidance.inspection: Identify an affirmative operational exception or automatic-copy authorization. Do not treat a consent-conditioned prohibition, employee access, a reference to existing copies, or a retention-only carve-out as this condition.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative creation exception or the automatic-copy acknowledgement with its permission, and retain purpose, access, confidentiality, and duration limits.

guidance.when: The source expressly prohibits making copies and offers only later consent or approval as a release, with no affirmative operational copying exception or permitted automatic-copy process.
guidance.inspection: Read the whole copy clause and adjacent exceptions. A possible future waiver of a prohibition is not present permission to create copies; verify that no stated-purpose, necessity, or automatic-backup exception changes the polarity.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative copying prohibition and its consent or approval condition, plus adjacent language needed to show whether any affirmative exception exists.
